title: Clarify firstmate study page jargon, diagram, tags and card titles
summary: Address the newcomer's rating findings on the firstmate study page (audience: newcomers reading the published page). Edit the page text in studies/firstmate-work-handling/intro.json and the renderer in xtask/src/site.rs: define terms where first used, add a 'home' entry, split 'agent' into two terms, explain the t10 ready→ready merge, title ra1–ra6, relabel the reopened tag, and explain or remove the study id. Leave the opening and Next steps unchanged.

defaults_applied.how: Page generator changes are in Rust (xtask/src/site.rs); content stays in the existing JSON data.
Update xtask site tests and require cargo test, clippy and fmt --check to pass.
New explanatory sentences cite existing claim ids so the page's claim-citation rule still holds.
Wording is written for a newcomer with no knowledge of firstmate.
Criteria check what the reader sees on the rendered page, not that fields exist.
One focused edit of the page text and renderer; no schema change.
Terms are defined at first use and the ambiguous term is split, rather than patching single sentences.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The published page is generated by xtask/src/site.rs from studies/firstmate-work-handling/*.json; the site is rebuilt on deploy, so no generated HTML is edited.
Rationale records reject unknown fields (deny_unknown_fields), so ra1–ra6 titles are added as a new list in intro.json read by site.rs rather than in rationales.json or the schema.
model.json state kinds (terminal-success) are validated study data and stay unchanged; the page shows a clearer display label and/or a short explanation for reopened.
The deciding part of firstmate keeps one name and workers get another (for example 'judgment' vs 'worker'); 'decided by agent' on cards is rendered with the deciding-part term and explained.
t10's ready→ready arrow is explained in the page text from the cited claims, not by changing model.json, unless the cited claims show the diagram is wrong.
Claims cited in new or changed sentences must come from existing claim ids; no new claims are invented.
The study id in the lede is removed or replaced with a plain-language explanation; the pin line stays.

acceptance_criteria.text: In 'Start here', 'captain' and 'yolo' are each defined in plain words at or before their first use, so a newcomer reading top to bottom meets no undefined term in that section.
The glossary has an entry for 'home' (firstmate home) that makes the secondmate and backlog item definitions understandable.
The glossary and the cards use two distinct terms for firstmate's deciding part and for the workers, and the page states which one 'decided by' refers to; the word 'agent' is no longer used for both.
The t10 card (or the page text near it) explains why a yolo merge is shown as ready → ready while t4 leads to done, or the diagram is corrected consistently with the cited claims.
Each of the six design-choice cards (ra1–ra6) has a short topic title in its heading alongside the id.
The reopened state no longer displays a bare 'terminal-success' tag that implies finished work; the label or an adjacent note says the item stays open waiting for the captain.
The lede no longer shows the raw study identifier without explanation; it is explained or removed. The opening paragraphs and the Next steps section keep their current wording.

Run `cargo test` (including xtask site tests, updated for any heading or text changes) and `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: all pass, and the real-study render test still passes with every cited claim id resolving.

out_of_scope: Changing the studied claims, sources, or the pinned firstmate commit
Changing the study record schema or validation rules in crates/athena-cap-study
Rewriting the opening paragraphs or the Next steps section
Editing records/ including the audience rating
Changes to site styling beyond what the new titles need
departures: Seven separate edits across data and renderer, with citation and validation constraints on new text, make verification slightly less likely to pass than the reference.
